MiniMaxH3MasterNode.summary: Authors and generates a timeline of MiniMax H3 shots with video and audio.
MiniMaxH3MasterNode.when: Use this as the centre of a normal workflow.
behavior: Reads the timeline, settings and each shot’s media assignments. Resolves a model family and prompt for each shot.
For text, opening/closing-frame and still-image modes, uses FL2VA. REF2VA, V2V and RV2V use REF2VA. Connected family models are loaded lazily.
Generates a new take or reuses a matching saved take. Applies enabled SelfLift, Refine and FaceRefine stages, then assembles the requested output.
Clip-by-clip stops after one newly generated shot. Full-batch works through the sequence. Conditioning Guide Output emits the last shot’s conditioning and latent for an external sampler.
The Preview tab requests separate latest-clip or complete-sequence preview files from completed caches. It does not change the Output selection.
steps: Load the starter and select both diffusion models, CLIP type minimax, and the video/audio VAEs.
Edit a shot’s mode, duration, prompt, audio policy and references in the Shots tab.
Run the workflow and inspect Preview → Latest clip. Validate a take you accept.
Add a shot and choose independent or chained continuity. Set Output → Full Video for a complete downstream export.
wiring: Load CLIP → clip; video Load VAE → video_vae; audio Load VAE → audio_vae
images + audio + fps → Create Video → Save Video
notes: Generation is fixed at 24 fps. Canvas dimensions must be multiples of 32. Generated durations round to the 5 + 17k frame grid.
video is VHS_VIDEOINFO metadata, not a native VIDEO object. Use Create Video to package images and audio.

prompt_text accepts one prompt per nonblank line. External group inputs replace timeline shots; prompt_text overrides existing shot prompts in line order; shots beyond the supplied lines keep their prompts. With no shots, lines construct new shots.
timeline_data and builder_state are editor-managed JSON. Normal users edit the visible UI rather than those values.
Latest preview fits within 960 × 540; final exports use the configured generated frames. A cache contains completed takes, not an unfinished sampler step.
Conditioning Guide Output returns placeholder images/audio; use its conditioning and latent in an external sampling/decoding graph.
MiniMaxH3MasterNode.extra:
Shot editor

Move: drag a shot’s body left or right. The insertion marker shows its new position; image, video and audio assignments move with it. Shots stay joined without gaps. Move earlier / Move later buttons offer the same operation.

Resize: drag the shot’s right edge to change duration. Delete: click × on the shot or Delete Shot in its inspector, then confirm. The last shot can be deleted; use + Add Shot to start again. A locked source stays in place. Reordering or deleting clears approval on affected later shots so chained output is regenerated.

Use Director Settings for size, steps, seed, execution and continuity. Use the Master for shots, prompts, references and review.

  • Keep a fixed seed while comparing a setting. Increment, decrement or randomize requests the next variation.
  • Only selected shots are generated when Generate selected shots is enabled. Unselected source ranges can pass through unchanged.
  • Validate a completed take to approve it. Reuse also requires matching inputs and files; changing a chained shot can invalidate its successors.
  • Generation uses a 24 fps frame grid: 5, 22, 39, 56, 73… frames. Width and height must be multiples of 32.

All-in-One Generation is the usual execution mode. Clip-by-clip stops after one new shot; full-batch processes the sequence. Manual resolution uses your dimensions, Auto uses aspect and megapixels, and Original snaps the source dimensions to the grid. Active working-resolution overrides take precedence.

Prompts and shot LoRAs

  • Example: A cyclist turns onto a wet street. Low tracking camera. Evening shop lights. Tires hiss on pavement.
  • Use raw text or structured editing; shared text supplies recurring instructions.
  • Mention selected media with the editor’s reference tokens. Check resolved_prompt to see what H3 receives.
  • Attach up to 8 LoRAs per shot.
  • Start with a moderate strength; compare with the same seed.
  • LoRAs modify the model; reference assets and RefMods supply media.

References and timed guides

Add & prepare reference media

  • Trim video/audio by start/end seconds; choose video, audio or both. The waveform shows decoded audio peaks.
  • Crop images/video using the rectangle or numeric fields. Scale with Off / Auto / Target / Fit / Fill; crop or pad to the required grid.
  • Set role and description. Subject/place/style/keyframe/pose are descriptive labels; pose is not a skeleton ControlNet.

Use RefMods & bundles

  • Use <RefMod 1> or <RefMod 1:memberName> to mention a bundle/member.
  • Expanded members count toward the normal reference limits.
  • RefMods organize reference assets; this node does not train or create a new RefMod model.

Place a guide at a time

  • Enter the guide time in seconds inside the visible shot.
  • The native AddGuide path offsets the anchor for a continuity prefix.
  • Check the reference and timestamp when an anchor lands at the wrong point.

Limits: 9 images, 3 videos, 3 audios, 12 combined; each reference video and their total duration must be ≤15 seconds. Native H3 may impose additional combination constraints. Crops retain the original asset; picking a source frame uses the original player time.

This is a timestamped native guide, not an additional guide-strength control.

Source-video editing

  • Use V2V/RV2V and describe the desired edit. The source becomes reference Video 1.
  • Split at the playhead, split equally or use optional scene detection. Merge only contiguous ranges from the same file.
  • Leave other ranges unselected for source passthrough; generated ranges are trimmed to the source length.

There is no generic source-latent strength slider. Automatic continuity prefixes are disabled for source edits. Scene detection needs scenedetect[opencv]. To extend a video, use locked source Clip 0, then add generated shots. Source ranges keep original-time coordinates.

Project files and recovery

  • Workflow JSON: graph and node settings. Lightweight project JSON: timeline/settings with asset and cache hints.
  • Portable .mmxproj: includes reference/source bytes; excludes models and heavy generated takes.
  • Append remaps incoming IDs; overwrite replaces authoring. New Project / Reset Timeline / Clear Cache have different scopes.

Clear Cache removes generated takes while retaining uploaded assets. Appended shared references become local to imported shots. Back up generated-take storage separately when moving servers.
output_descriptions: Assembled RGB frames for the Output selection.
Matching audio for the returned frame sequence.
VHS_VIDEOINFO timing/dimension metadata; not a playable native VIDEO.
Final shot conditioning for an external sampling graph.
Final shot H3 joint audiovisual latent.
Number of frames in the returned assembled IMAGE batch.
JSON run report with generated/reused shot details.
Updated authoring timeline JSON, including shot seed state.

MiniMaxH3DirectorSettings.summary: Builds the canvas, sampling and execution configuration consumed by the Master.
MiniMaxH3DirectorSettings.when: Use this in every ordinary starter workflow.
behavior: Returns one configuration dictionary. This node does not sample or decode media.
The Master uses this configuration as its baseline; active timeline resolution controls can override width and height.
When settings_optional is connected, incoming values take precedence over this node’s values.
steps: Connect config to the Master config socket.
For a first run, use the starter’s 960 × 544, 24 fps, 25 steps, CFG 1, euler/simple and fixed seed.
Choose All-in-One Generation, then clip_by_clip or full_batch.
Set Independent for separate scenes, or a continuity mode for a sequence.
notes: The newly created node defaults to res_multistep, structured prompting and chained continuity. The starter intentionally uses different initial selections.
context_length choices are pixel-frame context lengths, despite the legacy tooltip mentioning latent frames.
Changing export playback FPS uses Output Processing; the Master generation frame_rate must stay at 24.

control_descriptions.context_length: Continuity context length in pixel frames: 5, 22, 39 or 56. This is unrelated to language-model context tokens.

output_descriptions: Configuration consumed by the Master config input.

MiniMaxH3DirectorSelfLift.summary: Configures a low-resolution sampling stage followed by a full-resolution finish.
MiniMaxH3DirectorSelfLift.when: Use it to try reducing the cost of high-resolution sampling.
behavior: Returns a settings pack; the Master applies it during sampling.
lowres_scale changes the initial spatial size. split_mode chooses a fixed number of final high-resolution steps or a transition step.
The visual latent is enlarged between stages. Optional native low-resolution carry supports compatible chained shots; rho enables a pixel-anchor mixing path.
steps: Connect selflift to the Master selflift socket.
Start with lowres_scale 0.5 and highres_steps 4.
Use follow_director if you want the main sampler selection; euler selects the SelfLift sampler path.
Compare a fixed-seed baseline before trying learned weights, tiling, chunks or anchor mixing.
notes: Missing learned upscaler weights fall back to interpolation; this node has no explicit interpolate item in its weight dropdown.
model_hires affects only the high-resolution stage and must be compatible with the shot family.
MiniMaxH3DirectorSelfLift.extra: The weight dropdown has no explicit “interpolate” entry: when no weights are installed, its unset placeholder falls back to interpolation. native_low_carry reuses compatible low-resolution context only for chained shots. rho=0 disables the optional pixel-anchor mix; w_min/w_max bound its weighting.

MiniMaxH3DirectorRefine.summary: Configures latent refinement or enlargement after the first sampling pass.
MiniMaxH3DirectorRefine.when: Use it for another detail pass or to enlarge visual latents.
behavior: refine adds a sampling pass without requiring enlargement. upscale enlarges then refines. latent_upscale enlarges without diffusion.
passes repeats the configured refinement. Optional refine_model and sigmas override the model and noise schedule for this stage.
The global backend uses memory-aware planning. The sampler backend uses explicit spatial tile settings. Audio is not spatially enlarged.
steps: Connect refine to the Master refine socket.
Start with enabled, mode refine, one pass, 3 steps and denoise 0.45.
For enlargement, select target dimensions and interpolation or compatible H3 latent weights.
Enable tiles/chunks when needed and compare detail and motion before increasing passes.
wiring: Optional MODEL → refine_model; optional SIGMAS → sigmas
notes: Learned weights must match the supported 24-channel H3 3D architecture; image upscaler weights are not interchangeable.
SIGMAS must be a finite, nonnegative, nonincreasing 1D schedule with at least two values.
More passes can increase compute and drift.
MiniMaxH3DirectorRefine.extra:
Optional refine_model must be compatible. SIGMAS must be 1D, finite, nonnegative and nonincreasing, with ≥2 entries. More passes (1–20) cost compute and can drift.

Supported checkpoint extensions: .safetensors, .sft, .pt, .pth. Loading validates architecture. Audio stays separate from visual latent enlargement.

control_descriptions.backend: global uses memory-aware refinement planning; sampler uses the native sampler path with explicit tiles.

MiniMaxH3DirectorFaceRefine.summary: Configures detection, tracking and refinement of one face in decoded video.
MiniMaxH3DirectorFaceRefine.when: Use it when one face needs repair while retaining the main shot and audio.
behavior: Selects an initial largest or centre-most face and tracks it across frames.
Samples face crops with native H3 audiovisual conditioning, then pastes the refined pixels using the chosen region, feathering, colour match and blend.
Keeps the main audio. No face detections produce a reported skip; a missing detector is a setup error.
steps: Install the detector file in models/ultralytics/bbox and its required detector dependencies.
Connect face_refine to the Master face_refine socket.
Start with the default prompt, strength 0.35 and crop_size 512.
Inspect tracking and stitching before changing crop_factor, paste_region or sampling controls.
notes: Tracks one face, not all faces. blend 0 preserves the original frames.
Manual versus capped-auto canvas controls the face crop, not the entire video size.
MiniMaxH3DirectorFaceRefine.extra: Tracks one face, samples native audiovisual crops and keeps the main audio. No detections means a reported skip; a missing detector is a setup error. Inherit or offset the shot seed; stitching fades edits near boundaries.

MiniMaxH3DirectorSemanticBridge.summary: Builds a configuration for adapting the text-conditioning tokens with a student network.
MiniMaxH3DirectorSemanticBridge.when: Use it only when you have the matching Semantic Bridge checkpoint.
behavior: The node packs a checkpoint selection and alpha. The Master applies the student rewrite to conditioning.
The student maps 5120-dimensional tokens through a 512-dimensional hidden representation. alpha controls the mix with the original tokens.
steps: Place compatible student weights in models/semantic_bridge.
Select the checkpoint, start with alpha 0.15, and connect semantic_bridge to the Master.
Compare against the same seed without the bridge.
notes: This is a conditioning adapter, not a LoRA or a reference image encoder.
The exact architecture and tensor keys are validated; arbitrary checkpoints are unsuitable.

MiniMaxH3Cache.summary: Patches an H3 model to reuse approximate block-stack residuals during sampling.
MiniMaxH3Cache.when: Use it when you want to test a quality/speed tradeoff.
behavior: Clones the input model and installs a residual reuse hook. It returns a MODEL, not a configuration or a saved-take cache.
Reuse is active only between start_percent and end_percent and for at most max_steps consecutive skips.
Reuse threshold controls accumulated residual-change tolerance; larger values permit more approximation. State resets for each sampling run.
steps: Insert it after a Load Diffusion Model and before the corresponding Master family-model input.
Start with threshold 0.05, start 0.15, end 0.90 and max_steps 2.
Compare motion against an unpatched model with the same seed.
wiring: Load Diffusion Model MODEL → Cache model
Cache MODEL → Master fl2va_model or ref2va_model
notes: Requires the supported MiniMaxH3Model block layout. start_percent must not exceed end_percent.
Can introduce ghosting or temporal smearing. It does not provide saved-take persistence, and no measured speedup is promised.
output_descriptions: Cloned H3 model with the residual-reuse hooks installed.

MiniMaxH3DirectorGroupImageToVideo.summary: Packs one text/keyframe shot for the Master from graph inputs.
MiniMaxH3DirectorGroupImageToVideo.when: Use it when another graph provides a prompt or endpoint images.
behavior: With no endpoint images it creates a text shot. first_frame creates I2V; both endpoints create FL2V; last_frame alone creates L2V.
Returns an MMX_DIR_GROUP object. It does not sample or decode anything.
steps: Set prompt and duration_sec.
Optionally connect first_frame and/or last_frame.
Connect group to Master i2v_groups, or combine several groups first.
notes: External groups replace the editor’s shot list for that execution. Keep ordinary UI shots and graph-authored groups as deliberate alternatives.
The Master converts external groups into independent shots with continuity disabled.

MiniMaxH3DirectorGroupReferenceToVideo.summary: Packs one REF2VA shot with graph-supplied images, video frames and audio.
MiniMaxH3DirectorGroupReferenceToVideo.when: Use it for a reference-driven graph-authored shot.
behavior: Collects connected image slots, a video-frame batch and audio into one reference-family group.
Prompt, duration and reference image-size policy are preserved for Master execution.
steps: Set a prompt and duration_sec.
Connect a visual reference; optional audio references need a visual reference alongside them.
Connect group to Master r2v_groups, directly or through Groups Combine.
wiring: IMAGE → ref_image_1; optional frame batch → ref_video_1; AUDIO → ref_audio_1
notes: ref_images uses the separate REF_PACK type. It is not compatible with this pack’s MMX_REF_PACK output; use individual image inputs for normal graph wiring.
Native REF2VA reference-count and duration constraints still apply.
The Master converts external groups into independent shots with continuity disabled.

MiniMaxH3DirectorGroupsCombine.summary: Flattens connected shot groups into a single ordered group list.
MiniMaxH3DirectorGroupsCombine.when: Use it to put several graph-authored shots into one Master group input.
behavior: Reads group_1 through group_10 in numeric order. Each input may contain one group or a list; lists are flattened.
Fails when no group is connected. This is shot-data assembly, not frame or video concatenation.
steps: Create Image-to-Video or Reference-to-Video group nodes.
Connect them in your intended order to group_1, group_2 and so on.
Connect groups to the appropriate Master group input.
notes: The Master processes a directly connected i2v_groups list before a directly connected r2v_groups list. A single combined list keeps its own order.

MiniMaxH3RefPack.summary: Pools graph-supplied references for local selection on individual Master shots.
MiniMaxH3RefPack.when: Use it when references come from other nodes; ordinary uploaded references can use the Master directly.
behavior: Adds up to four image inputs, two video-frame batches, two audio inputs and two RefMod names per pack.
ref_pack_optional inherits an earlier pool. Chained packs receive distinct identifiers so slots do not collide.
Pooling makes assets available; the Master’s shot selections decide which assets enter each shot.
steps: Connect reference media to the matching sockets.
Chain pools through ref_pack_optional if more graph inputs are needed.
Connect ref_pack to Master ref_pack, press Sync Refs, and assign assets to the intended shot.
wiring: Earlier pool ref_pack → next pool ref_pack_optional
notes: The pool can grow through chaining, but each shot still obeys native limits: 9 images, 3 videos, 3 audios, 12 combined.
A video input is an IMAGE frame batch. RefMods are names/paths or bundles, not newly trained models.
output_descriptions: Reference pool with asset identifiers and pack count.

MiniMaxH3TailFromLatent.summary: Decodes a sampled H3 joint audiovisual latent and returns its ending frames and audio.
MiniMaxH3TailFromLatent.when: Use it for manual sampler graphs that need a continuation tail.
behavior: Decodes the full latent with the video/audio VAEs, then selects the final tail_seconds of media.
When alignment is enabled, selects a nearby valid H3 frame-grid length within the available frames.
Returns the tail frame batch, matching tail audio, last frame, frame count and duration.
steps: Connect a sampled H3 LATENT, the video VAE and the audio VAE.
Start with tail_seconds 0.5 and grid alignment enabled.
Use ref_video and ref_video_audio as manual continuation references, or last_frame as an endpoint image.
wiring: Video VAE → vae; Audio VAE → audio_vae
notes: This performs decoding again; use Load Take Checkpoint when you already have a durable completed take.
video_vae is an optional alias that takes precedence over vae.
output_descriptions: Audio sliced to the tail duration.
Final decoded frame as a one-frame batch.

MiniMaxH3VideoCombine.summary: Encodes an IMAGE frame batch and optional audio with advanced codec controls.
MiniMaxH3VideoCombine.when: Use it instead of the stock output pair when you need these export options.
behavior: Encodes frames using PyAV by default, or the explicit FFmpeg backend.
Supports codec/container choices, bit depth, audio codec/bitrate, metadata, ping-pong, crop-to-audio and optional first/last stills.
Writes to output or temp according to save_output. The UI displays a video preview; frames are returned only when pass_frames is enabled.
steps: Connect Master images and audio; set frame_rate to the Master fps.
For a compatibility baseline, choose H.264, mp4, 8-bit and save_output true.
Set filename_prefix and run the workflow.
Use the returned filename or ComfyUI history to locate/download the video.
wiring: Master images → images; Master audio → audio
Master fps → frame_rate (convert the widget to an input when wiring)
notes: filename is a path STRING, not a native VIDEO. Use stock Create Video / Save Video for the simplest starter.
Codec support depends on installed encoders. Animated output requires PyAV. pass_frames does not turn off encoding.
The browser fallback preview can be H.264 even when the saved file uses another codec.
output_descriptions: Processed frame batch when pass_frames is enabled; otherwise an empty batch.
Encoded file path as a STRING.

MiniMaxH3ModelOverridePack.summary: Registers named model overrides for individual shots.
MiniMaxH3ModelOverridePack.when: Use it when shots need compatible models different from the main family models.
behavior: Copies previous entries, then adds the stripped name and MODEL.
Using the same name replaces that entry. The Master resolves a shot’s model_override by that name.
steps: Load a compatible diffusion model and choose a meaningful name.
Chain additional entries through previous.
Connect the pack to Master model_pack and select that named model on a shot.
notes: Names must not be blank. The model must remain compatible with the shot family, encoders and VAEs.
SelfLift model_hires and Refine refine_model are separate stage-specific overrides.

MiniMaxH3Checkpoint.summary: Loads a complete saved take from a project’s server-side cache.
MiniMaxH3Checkpoint.when: Use it to resume or branch from an already completed shot.
behavior: latest selects the current take for clip_id. An explicit take UUID selects that historical generation from the manifest.
Loads the saved latent, decoded frames and audio. Fails if any required artifact is missing or unreadable.
Returns a continuation object plus separate media and latent outputs; it does not generate a new take.
steps: Find the project ID, shot ID and optional take UUID in the Master’s saved-take tools.
Enter those values and load the checkpoint.
Connect checkpoint to another Master continuation input to branch or continue.
wiring: frames / audio → export nodes if you only want the saved media
notes: Project and shot IDs are cache identifiers, not the shot’s display name.
Cache files must remain on the same server or be restored. Portable reference archives exclude heavy generated-take storage.
output_descriptions: Complete take with identifiers, latent, frames and audio.

MiniMaxH3AdvanceCheckpoint.summary: Chooses explicitly between a current and a staged continuation checkpoint.
MiniMaxH3AdvanceCheckpoint.when: Use it as a manual gate when reviewing a proposed new take.
behavior: advance false returns current. advance true returns staged.
It does not compare quality, generate takes or change the stored project manifest.
steps: Load two complete checkpoints and connect current and staged.
Keep advance false while evaluating the staged take.
Set advance true when you want downstream continuation to use staged.
wiring: Current checkpoint → current; proposed checkpoint → staged
notes: Both inputs are ordinary required graph inputs; this node is not a lazy execution gate that prevents upstream generation.
output_descriptions: current or staged, selected by the advance boolean.

MiniMaxH3PromptForge.summary: Asks a local or server-accessible language model for a structured prompt draft.
MiniMaxH3PromptForge.when: Use it to draft several shots before manually accepting them.
behavior: Reads the timeline snapshot and instruction, requests shot_count draft shots, and records the source context.
Optional images are encoded for a provider that supports vision. No video generation occurs.
Returns an editable draft object and review_json text; the draft is not applied automatically.
steps: Supply a timeline snapshot and describe the intended scenes in instruction.
Choose local with a connected generator, or configure an Ollama/compatible endpoint and model.
Inspect review_json, then connect draft to Review / Apply Prompt Draft.
wiring: Local Prompt / Vision Model → generator (local backend)
draft → Review / Apply Prompt Draft draft
notes: Provider requests originate from the ComfyUI server. localhost refers to that server.
Graph api_key fields can be saved in workflow JSON. Stale drafts are rejected on application if the source context changed.
Do not wire a Master output back into that same Master through a cyclic draft graph; use an independent snapshot or the editor draft flow.

control_descriptions.backend: local uses a connected generator; ollama or compatible sends requests to the selected endpoint.
control_descriptions.images: Up to 12 visual inputs encoded for a provider that supports vision.

MiniMaxH3ApplyPromptDraft.summary: Applies an accepted prompt draft to a timeline snapshot.
MiniMaxH3ApplyPromptDraft.when: Use it after reviewing a Prompt Forge result.
behavior: apply false returns the original timeline string unchanged.
apply true verifies the draft’s source context and applies replace or append, returning updated timeline JSON.
steps: Supply the same timeline snapshot used for drafting and connect the draft.
Review the draft and choose replace or append.
Set apply true, then use the returned STRING as the Master timeline_data input.
wiring: Prompt Forge draft → draft; matching timeline JSON → timeline
notes: Replacing changes the authored shot list; appending adds draft shots. This does not render them.
A returned timeline JSON is not a line-per-shot prompt_text string. Use the timeline_data input.

MiniMaxH3LocalPromptModel.summary: Loads an installed local text or vision model for Prompt Forge.
MiniMaxH3LocalPromptModel.when: Use it with the local draft backend.
behavior: Loads a complete Transformers directory or GGUF file from models/LLM and caches a provider for the selected options.
Transformers uses local files only. GGUF uses llama-cpp-python; vision also needs a matching projection file.
Returns a callable LLM pipeline, not H3 CLIP conditioning or a diffusion MODEL.
steps: Place a compatible model directory or GGUF file in models/LLM.
Choose backend, device and context_length.
For vision, enable vision and provide the necessary projection with GGUF.
Connect the pipeline to Prompt Forge generator and set its backend to local.
notes: Weights are not downloaded automatically. CUDA uses additional GPU memory.
The backend and vision options must match the chosen model; the node does not convert an arbitrary text model into a vision model.

control_descriptions.backend: transformers loads a complete local model directory; gguf loads a local GGUF file.
control_descriptions.device: CPU or CUDA placement for this local language model.
control_descriptions.context_length: Context size for the local model, unrelated to video continuity frames.

MiniMaxH3ProjectVideo.summary: Exports cached project shots one at a time and assembles a native VIDEO file.
MiniMaxH3ProjectVideo.when: Use it for individual-shot export or rebuilding a saved sequence without resampling.
behavior: Reads the project ID from timeline first, otherwise from the project_id widget. Iterates shots in timeline order, optionally only selected shots.
final uses cached final frames; pre_refine uses the saved first-pass frames; original_source decodes source ranges. Locked shots use their sources.
Applies stored context/handoff trims, normalizes canvases, adjusts output FPS and audio, encodes shots, then concatenates their files with FFmpeg.
Returns a native VIDEO, individual shot-file JSON and an assembled UI preview.
steps: Connect Master project_state to timeline, or supply a saved timeline JSON.
Choose all/selected, stream, fps and filename_prefix.
Enable export_individual_shots when you want permanent per-shot files as well.
Run after the needed takes and source media are available.
wiring: Returned VIDEO → optional native VIDEO consumer
notes: Requires FFmpeg for assembly and H.264 MP4 encoding support. It also writes an assembled output itself.
Missing final/pre-refine media can fall back to a source range when one exists; otherwise export fails.
Changing FPS repeats/drops frames; it does not add AI motion interpolation.
The assembled file is already written by this node; Save Video is only needed if you intentionally want another saved copy.
output_descriptions: Native VIDEO backed by the assembled file.
JSON list of encoded individual shot files.

MiniMaxH3OutputProcessing.summary: Changes decoded playback timing, adds a watermark and optionally creates a loop.
MiniMaxH3OutputProcessing.when: Use it between the Master and a video encoder.
behavior: resample repeats/drops frames to preserve duration at playback_fps. retime changes duration and audio pitch.
Applies a logo or text watermark; a connected logo takes precedence over text.
A positive loop overlap crossfades the end into the beginning and shortens the sequence by that overlap. Returns processed frames, audio and playback FPS.
steps: Connect Master images, audio and fps as source_fps.
Choose playback_fps and policy; leave rates equal for no timing change.
Set watermark text or connect a logo, then choose corner and opacity.
Use loop_overlap_frames only when a loop is needed; connect all three processed outputs to the encoder.
wiring: Master images / audio / fps → images / audio / source_fps
IMAGE / AUDIO / FLOAT → Create Video images / audio / fps
notes: Resampling is not optical-flow or AI frame interpolation. Retime changes pitch.
Loop overlap must be less than half the frame count. For example, 124 frames with a 12-frame overlap produces 112 frames.
output_descriptions: Processed/fitted audio, or no audio if none was supplied.
Playback FPS to pass to the encoder.

MiniMaxH3PixelUpscale.summary: Resizes decoded frames with bicubic, learned image upscaling or optional NVIDIA RTX effects.
MiniMaxH3PixelUpscale.when: Use it after generation when you need larger pixel output.
behavior: bicubic resizes directly. learned_pixel first invokes an UPSCALE_MODEL, then resizes to the exact width and height.
Those two paths can stretch the aspect ratio; resize_method applies to RTX providers.
RTX paths require CUDA and the optional NVIDIA effects runtime. They can run denoise/deblur before the chosen VSR or High Bitrate effect.
Returns processed IMAGE frames only. Audio and timing are passed separately to the exporter.
steps: Connect Master images to images.
Start with bicubic and a target matching the original aspect ratio.
For learned_pixel, connect a stock-loaded UPSCALE_MODEL.
Send output frames to Create Video while keeping the original Master audio and fps connections.
wiring: Master images → images; IMAGE output → Create Video images
Master audio + fps → Create Video audio + fps
notes: This operates on pixels, not the H3 latent. Learned image weights do not belong in Refine’s latent_upscale_model selector.
RTX settings have no effect on bicubic/learned_pixel paths. Missing RTX dependencies or hardware produce an error.

control_descriptions.quality: RTX provider quality preset; not the video encoder’s CRF quality.

control_descriptions.images: Decoded RGB frame batch, in playback order.
control_descriptions.audio: Waveform and sample rate belonging to the supplied frames.
control_descriptions.model: Diffusion MODEL to modify or register.
control_descriptions.prompt: Text used for this shot or refinement stage.
control_descriptions.steps: Number of diffusion steps for this stage.
control_descriptions.sigmas: Optional explicit noise schedule; takes precedence over the generated schedule.
control_descriptions.enabled: Enable this processing stage when the Master runs.
control_descriptions.device: Where the provider or its reusable data is held.
control_descriptions.timeline: Authoring timeline as a JSON string, including project and shot identifiers.
control_descriptions.project_id: Server cache project identifier. On Project Export, the timeline’s project_id takes precedence.
control_descriptions.clip_id: Saved shot identifier, such as clip_1; not its display name.
control_descriptions.take_id: latest for the current take, or a saved take UUID for a specific historical result.
control_descriptions.latent_upscale_model: Compatible learned H3 latent upscaler weights. Refine also offers interpolate; SelfLift falls back to interpolation when no usable weights are selected.
control_descriptions.enable_latent_chunking: Process learned visual-latent enlargement in temporal chunks to limit working memory.
control_descriptions.enable_tiling: Use spatial tiles for the supported sampling path.
control_descriptions.tile_count: Number of spatial tiles along the configured tile layout.
control_descriptions.tile_overlap: Overlap between spatial tiles; blended to reduce boundaries.
control_descriptions.split_mode: Choose the high-resolution switch by final-step count or by transition_step.
control_descriptions.transition_step: Sampling step at which the high-resolution stage begins when that split mode is selected.
control_descriptions.sampler_mode: euler uses the SelfLift path; follow_director follows the main sampler.
control_descriptions.rho: Strength of the optional VAE pixel-anchor mix. Zero disables it.
control_descriptions.w_min: Lower bound for pixel-anchor mix weighting.
control_descriptions.w_max: Upper bound for pixel-anchor mix weighting.
control_descriptions.latent_upsample: Interpolation method used for visual latent enlargement.
control_descriptions.model_hires: Optional compatible MODEL used only for the high-resolution SelfLift stage.
control_descriptions.memory_budget_mb: Memory budget used by the global refinement planner; zero selects automatic handling.
control_descriptions.upscale_precision: Numerical precision for learned latent enlargement.
control_descriptions.strength: Sampling strength for the tracked face crop.
control_descriptions.confidence: Minimum detector confidence for a face candidate.
control_descriptions.crop_factor: How much surrounding context is included around the detected face.
control_descriptions.canvas_mode: Use the manual crop canvas or a capped automatic crop canvas.
control_descriptions.select: Select the initial largest face or the face nearest the centre.
control_descriptions.paste_region: Restrict the pasted result to a face rectangle, an ellipse, or the full crop.
control_descriptions.mask_dilation: Expand the pasted face region by this many pixels.
control_descriptions.feather: Soften the pasted boundary over this many pixels.
control_descriptions.colour_match: Strength of matching the refined crop to the base shot’s colour.
control_descriptions.blend: Amount of refined pixels pasted onto the base; zero preserves the base.
control_descriptions.seed_mode: Inherit the shot seed or use the refinement offset policy.
control_descriptions.reuse_threshold: Tolerance for accumulated residual changes. Larger values allow more approximate reuse.
control_descriptions.start_percent: Fraction of the sampling run at which residual reuse becomes active.
control_descriptions.end_percent: Fraction of the sampling run after which residual reuse stops.
control_descriptions.verbose: Log residual reuse statistics for troubleshooting.
control_descriptions.ref_image_size: Reference image sizing policy passed to the Master’s group resolver.
control_descriptions.samples: Sampled MiniMax H3 joint video/audio LATENT dictionary.
control_descriptions.tail_seconds: Requested duration of the decoded ending tail.
control_descriptions.align_to_h3_grid: Select a nearby valid 5 + 17k tail-frame count within the available frames.
control_descriptions.frame_rate: Frames per second for the encoded video; use the timing of the supplied frames.
control_descriptions.codec: Video codec to encode. Auto resolves a compatible available choice.
control_descriptions.encoder_backend: PyAV encoder path or explicit FFmpeg fallback.
control_descriptions.quality: Encoder quality parameter; lower H.264/H.265 CRF values mean higher quality and larger files.
control_descriptions.pingpong: Append a reversed sequence, excluding duplicate endpoints.
control_descriptions.save_metadata: Include available workflow/prompt metadata in the output.
control_descriptions.filename_prefix: Output path/name prefix, relative to the selected output or temp folder.
control_descriptions.save_output: Write permanent output when true; write temporary output when false.
control_descriptions.pass_frames: Return the processed frames on the frames output. Encoding still runs when false.
control_descriptions.crop_to_audio: Stop video at the supplied audio duration when shorter.
control_descriptions.audio_codec: Audio codec used when audio is provided.
control_descriptions.audio_bitrate: Target encoded audio bitrate where supported.
control_descriptions.save_first_frame: Write the first encoded frame as an additional still image.
control_descriptions.save_last_frame: Write the last encoded frame as an additional still image.
control_descriptions.seed: Optional connected seed for output metadata and supported encoder behavior.
control_descriptions.name: Nonblank name used to select this model override on a shot.
control_descriptions.previous: Previously built named-model pack. This entry is added to it, replacing the same name if present.
control_descriptions.current: Checkpoint returned while advance is false.
control_descriptions.staged: Checkpoint returned when advance is true.
control_descriptions.advance: Explicitly select staged instead of current.
control_descriptions.instruction: Describe the scenes and constraints the prompt provider should draft.
control_descriptions.shot_count: Number of draft shots to request.
control_descriptions.endpoint: Server-accessible provider URL; localhost refers to the ComfyUI host.
control_descriptions.model_name: Installed model/provider model identifier for the selected backend.
control_descriptions.api_key: Provider credential. A graph widget can be serialized into workflow JSON.
control_descriptions.draft: Prompt draft produced by Prompt Forge, with its source-context identity.
control_descriptions.apply: False preserves the original timeline; true applies the reviewed draft.
control_descriptions.policy: Replace the shot list or append the draft shots.
control_descriptions.vision: Enable the chosen local model’s supported vision path.
control_descriptions.projection: Matching GGUF vision projection filename under models/LLM.
control_descriptions.context_length: Maximum context size requested from the local language-model provider.
control_descriptions.stream: Export cached final frames, saved pre-refine frames, or the original source range.
control_descriptions.selection: Export all timeline shots or only those marked selected.
control_descriptions.fps: Output playback FPS; frame repetition/dropping preserves duration.
control_descriptions.export_individual_shots: Keep permanent encoded shot files as well as the assembled project video.
control_descriptions.source_fps: Frame rate of the incoming images.
control_descriptions.playback_fps: Frame rate for the returned processed sequence and its encoder.
control_descriptions.playback_policy: resample preserves duration by repeating/dropping frames; retime changes duration and audio pitch.
control_descriptions.watermark_text: Text drawn on frames when no logo is connected; blank means no text watermark.
control_descriptions.opacity: Watermark alpha from transparent to opaque.
control_descriptions.corner: Placement corner for the text or logo.
control_descriptions.loop_overlap_frames: Number of end/start frames crossfaded for a loop. Zero disables looping.
control_descriptions.logo: Optional image watermark; takes precedence over watermark_text.
control_descriptions.provider: Bicubic resizing, learned image upscaling, or optional NVIDIA RTX processing.
control_descriptions.resize_method: RTX aspect handling: crop to fill or letterbox to fit. Does not apply to bicubic/learned_pixel.
control_descriptions.denoise: Enable the optional RTX denoise effect before the main RTX effect.
control_descriptions.deblur: Enable the optional RTX deblur effect before the main RTX effect.
control_descriptions.upscale_model: Stock-loaded image UPSCALE_MODEL required by learned_pixel.
control_descriptions.timeline_data: Timeline JSON owned by the shot editor. Connect a reviewed timeline here for advanced graph authoring.
control_descriptions.builder_state: Serialized editor/project-tool state. Normal authoring manages this automatically.
